changes.before: Replace int& alias with int alias. What happens after alias = 9?
changes.after: Use a reference as another name for an existing value.

before: int& alias = score binds alias to the existing score object. It is another name for that object, not an independent copied integer.
alias = 9 changes score because both names access the same object. A reference must be initialized when declared.
After binding, assigning another value through alias does not make it refer to a different variable. It changes the object it already names.
int copy = score creates a separate value. Changing copy later does not change score.
Expected output or behavior: 9 3. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare a reference and a copied value side by side. Explain which assignment modifies the original without using addresses. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A reference is another name for an existing object. An object is a stored value in the program. int& alias = score makes alias refer to the same integer as score.
Assigning through alias changes the original integer. A reference must have a target when you create it.
Once this reference is bound to score, it keeps that target. An assignment through alias changes score; it does not attach alias to another variable.
int copy = score creates a separate integer with the same starting value. Later changes to score do not update copy.
The program prints 9 3. alias = 9 changes score to nine. copy keeps the three that was copied earlier.
The & in int& is part of the reference declaration. Removing it makes alias a separate int, so assigning to alias would leave score alone.

before.question: Replace int& alias with int alias. What happens after alias = 9?
choices: score stays 3 because alias is now a separate copied value.
score still becomes 9 because every variable name is a reference.
The compiler rejects all integer copies.
before.explanation: Removing & changes this declaration from an alias to an independent int.

after.question: Replace int& alias with int alias. What happens after alias = 9?
choices: score stays 3 because alias now holds a separate copy.
score becomes 9 because every variable is a reference.
The compiler rejects all integer copies.
after.explanation: Without &, alias is an independent int. Changing it does not change score.
